section_summary: This section comprises correspondence and memoranda from June 1940 to February 1941 concerning Japanese government officials, military officers, railway personnel, and academic researchers stationed in or departing from the United States. The records primarily consist of diplomatic notes from the Japanese Embassy and Japanese Chargé d'Affaires requesting Federal income tax exemptions and sailing permits under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for naval inspectors, language officers, railway officials, and scholars. They also contain formal State Department certifications of reciprocity directed to the Secretary of the Treasury, Treasury responses confirming tax-exempt treatment, and an Office of Naval Intelligence report concerning Japanese naval fuel inspection operations.

subfiles.about: Transmits an ONI report regarding the closure of the Japanese Naval Fuel Inspection Office in Los Angeles and the reported establishment of an oil inspection office in Mexico.
subfiles.from: E. B. Nixon, Captain, U.S. Navy, Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.summary: Naval Intelligence reports an unidentified Japanese man, after the Los Angeles fuel inspection office closed, said he was leaving for Mexico May 4, 1940 where an oil inspection office would open.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Regarding Japanese Naval Fuel Inspection Office in Los Angeles

subfiles.about: Informs the Department of State of the scheduled departure of Tamon Maeda, a technical expert of the Japanese Foreign Office assigned to The Japan Institute in New York, and requests tax exemption notifications.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Note No. 137: Foreign Office expert Tamon Maeda of the Japan Institute sails from San Francisco June 24, 1940 on the Asama Maru; asks notice to authorities.
subfiles.title: Note No. 137 from the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Departure of Tamon Maeda

subfiles.about: Certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Tamon Maeda is entitled to Federal income tax exemption on his official compensation.
subfiles.summary: Hull certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) for Tamon Maeda, confirming a June 12 telephone message.
subfiles.title: Letter to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Tamon Maeda
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Note No. 137 and informs the Japanese Ambassador that steps have been taken to issue a sailing permit and grant income tax exemption to Tamon Maeda.
subfiles.summary: State says Maeda's sailing permit and exemption request, telephoned June 12, was referred to authorities for prompt action.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Ambassador Concerning Sailing Permit and Tax Exemption for Tamon Maeda

subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: File copy of the State Department's note acknowledging Note No. 137 regarding Tamon Maeda's sailing permit and tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: File copy of State's note on Maeda: his June 12 sailing-permit request went to authorities with prompt action arranged.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Ambassador Concerning Sailing Permit and Tax Exemption for Tamon Maeda (Copy)

subfiles.about: Encloses Japanese Embassy Note No. 141 and certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Toshiyuki Mori.

subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials granting income tax exemption to Tamon Maeda.
